explanation: Vanilla is native to Mexico and Central America. Elsewhere growers pollinate each flower by hand, using a method found on Réunion by Edmond Albius, an enslaved boy.

claims.text: Vanilla is obtained from the cured seed pods of orchids of the genus Vanilla, mainly Vanilla planifolia.
Vanilla pods are not produced by a bean plant (legume), a palm or a lily, even though they are often called vanilla beans.
The vanilla orchid is native to Mexico and Central America.
Outside its native range, vanilla flowers are usually pollinated by hand.
The hand-pollination technique used for vanilla was devised on Réunion by Edmond Albius, an enslaved boy.
